invariants.evidence: One SWAP kernel remains authoritative; I17 adds only runtime-side optional energy composition.
The new runtime binding bundle performs no file, format, path, parser, or file-unit I/O.
Accepted water exchange, external thermal provenance, enthalpy parameters, and evaluated energy remain distinct data categories.
The binding bundle is candidate-scoped scratch/provenance and is not added to committed or restart physical state.
Binding storage is per active caller/runtime composition and can be discarded after candidate evaluation.
The logical bundle can later map to arrays/pools/batches; zero-capacity bundles allocate no record array.

I17 rejects disagreement between the caller-supplied binding token and bundle token plus sample ordinal. It does not yet prove that token belongs to the thermal candidate itself; authoritative candidate-token association is explicitly deferred to the next runtime workunit.
Bindings are cheap to rebuild and require no physical re-solve or committed-temperature history.
Evaluation consumes generic accepted sample intervals and imposes no day/month/year semantics.
No midnight or fixed coupling-window duration is introduced.

The implementation supports coupling-supplied thermal provenance behind an explicit caller token; it does not claim the later runtime association that binds that token authoritatively to one completed candidate.
Groundwater H/q interface contracts are byte-preserved and no thermal binding can alter interface water flux.
The binding module owns no Q/flux/exchange amount; energy uses the already accepted carrier water amount as sole mass authority.
No interface response sensitivity or tangent contract is changed.
No extra SWAP or external-component solve is performed to resolve donor temperature.
Compact optional bundles avoid heavy per-column solver instances and remain suitable for batched MultiSWAP use.
The implementation contains no MODFLOW-cell, tile fraction, or one-to-one groundwater mapping.
Deep-vadose identity remains outside SWAP; the bundle accepts only opaque provenance and donor temperature.
Thermal provenance neither stores nor transfers water and cannot alter mass-conserving component transitions.
Binding/evaluation is independent of the selected soil-water solver implementation.
I17 reuses the existing EB-I04 liquid-water sensible-enthalpy primitive and EB-I13 accepted carrier rather than duplicating physics.
No HeadCalc, Richards, Jacobian, or solver-internal arrays are referenced by the new module or route.
External donor provenance is an explicit optional composition input, not a performance policy that changes physics.
Missing thermal provenance remains bounded-cost fail-closed energy diagnostics and does not trigger unbounded hydrologic retries.
The original I15 evaluator remains public and is regression-qualified; reference hydrology is untouched.
Missing, duplicate, nonfinite, caller-token-mismatched, wrong-class, and extra bindings are explicit diagnosable outcomes. Candidate ownership of the token is not claimed here.
External thermal storage is allocated only when explicitly initialized with positive capacity; the old I15 route has no binding cost.
Runtime/coupler remains responsible for supplying and authoritatively associating opaque lineage/provenance and temperature; I17 does not know external system topology or source type.
No implicit MODFLOW, .swp, daily, local-temperature fallback, T_ref fallback, zero fallback, or interval-only matching is introduced.
This artifact explicitly audits all 30 architecture invariants and the I17 gate enforces exact IDs 1..30.
